items.rationale: Each model call is separate; the program resends the earlier messages and tool results as part of the new input. The model keeps no private store (b), does not learn in its weights during a run (c), and tools return results to the program, not the model (d).
Nothing carries between sessions unless the program saves it and loads it into the new context. Automatic memory of earlier chats is the misconception M3.
Context sizes are 1,000, 1,500, 2,000 and 2,500 tokens, which sum to 8,000. Answering 6,000 (1,000 + 4 x 500 + ...) or 4,000 counts the context once rather than resending it each call.

items.answer: It would cost far more, since the whole manual is billed on every call, and a long context can reduce the model's recall of the relevant part.
accepted: too many tokens and the model may miss the relevant part
items.rationale: Full credit names two reasons from: cost (tokens resent every call), context rot or reduced accuracy with long context, or hitting the window limit. One reason only is partial.

items.answer: A note is a fact the agent saves outside the context, so it can be read back later, including in a new session or after the context is trimmed.
accepted: a saved fact in storage that persists beyond the context window
information written to external storage and reloaded later
items.rationale: Full credit: information written to storage outside the context, which persists beyond one call or session. Describing it as something that stays in the context is wrong; the context is rebuilt and limited.
